Looking at each option:

(A) "a tribe valled quests" - Just a misspelling (valled instead of called, quests instead of quest)

(B) "a tribe callew quest" - Just a typo (callew instead of called)

(C) "a tribe called queso" - This replaces "quest" with "queso" (Spanish for cheese). This is humorous because it's a clever pun/wordplay - "queso" sounds phonetically similar to "quest" but means something completely different, creating an absurd and funny substitution.

(D) "a tribe callel quest" - Just a typo (callel instead of called)

The humorous edit is the one that creates wordplay, not just random misspellings. Option C is the only one with actual comedic intent through the pun substitution.

ANSWER: (C)
